superseded_instrument: UNWEIGHTED_MODULE_MEAN (v77_component_oracle_v3), retained on disk and readable
measured_on: the EXISTING generated worlds, so instrument change is isolated from generator change

ACCEPTANCE_GATE.rule: acceptable only if the intended positive signal is restored AND the negative controls still reject

B4.note: the designed band was set while the instrument under-read; with the correct statistic B4 exceeds it

C2.explicitly_not: a new C2 design attempt; the stopping-rule attempt count is unchanged at 3
C2.finding: C2's prior failure was INSTRUMENTAL. Its ratio statistic consumes the C2_local module score, which the unweighted mean under-read. On the exact same data with the unchanged band it now passes.

C3.note: unchanged by construction; C3's statistic is depth/support and does not use module scores

CONSEQUENCE_THE_WORLD_IS_TOO_EASY.observation: with the correct instrument the oracle ceilings sit between about 0.82 and 0.96 for most components, and the B6 ladder saturates at 0.73/0.93/0.95/0.96 against a designed 0.05/0.15/0.30/0.45/0.60
CONSEQUENCE_THE_WORLD_IS_TOO_EASY.reading: given known support AND known sign the planted structure is close to trivially recoverable. Several components are now OUTSIDE their designed classes by being too easy, not too hard.
CONSEQUENCE_THE_WORLD_IS_TOO_EASY.bearing_on_the_covariance_defect: this reinforces the review lane's priority. A world whose dependence structure is five-fold weaker than real RNA has little competing structure to hide a planted module in, so recoverability is inflated. The designed classes should be re-examined only AFTER the generator is recalibrated, never by moving a band now.

WHAT_THIS_DOES_NOT_DO: it does not promote these ceilings to decision evidence; the generator is still miscalibrated
it does not change any designed recoverability class or acceptance band
it does not verify S126, which needs the ATAC oracle under the same repair
it does not qualify any model; no model has been run
